en: Udāna 2.9 Visākhāsutta Thus have I heard:
On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in the Eastern Park, in the Mansion of Migāra’s Mother.
Now on that occasion Visākhā, Migāra’s Mother, had some business pending with King Pasenadi of Kosala,
but King Pasenadi of Kosala did not settle it according to her wishes.
Then Visākhā, Migāra’s mother, went to the Blessed One during the middle of the day; having approached and paid homage to the Blessed One, she sat down to one side.
As Visākhā, Migāra’s mother, was sitting there, the Blessed One said this to her:
“Well now, Visākhā, from where have you come, in the middle of the day?”
“Bhante, I have a certain matter here that depends on King Pasenadi of Kosala,
but King Pasenadi of Kosala does not resolve it according to my intention.
Then the Blessed One, having understood this matter, on that occasion uttered this inspired exclamation:
“Everything under the control of another is suffering;
everything under one’s own mastery is happiness.
Those who share [their wealth] with others are tormented.”
For the bonds are difficult to transcend.
